questions.question: A paper strip is folded into 8 equal parts. 3 of the parts are coloured blue and the other 5 parts are left white. Which ratio compares the blue parts to the white parts?
questions.explain: The word blue is named first, so the number of blue parts goes first: 3 : 5. The one that says 3 : 8 compares blue to the whole strip instead of blue to white, and 5 : 3 puts the two colours backwards.

questions.question: There are 10 counters on a desk. 4 of them are red and 6 of them are yellow. Which ratio compares the red counters to the yellow counters?
options: 4 to 10
4 to 6
6 to 4
10 to 6
questions.explain: A ratio lists the quantities in the order they are named, so red first: 4 to 6. The one that says 4 to 10 compares red to all the counters, which is a part-to-whole comparison, not red to yellow.

questions.question: A quilt square is made of 9 equal small squares. 2 of the small squares are green and the other 7 are white. Which ratio compares the white squares to the green squares?
questions.explain: White is named first, so the 7 white squares are written first: 7 : 2. Writing 2 : 7 answers a different question (green to white), and 9 : 7 uses the whole quilt square instead of just the green part.

questions.question: A tray is cut into 11 equal pieces of banana bread. 4 pieces have chocolate chips and the other 7 pieces are plain. The ratio 7 : 4 compares which two amounts?
options: chocolate chip pieces to plain pieces
plain pieces to all the pieces on the tray
all the pieces on the tray to chocolate chip pieces
plain pieces to chocolate chip pieces
questions.explain: In 7 : 4 the first number is 7, and 7 is the number of plain pieces, so it compares plain to chocolate chip. Reading it as chocolate chip to plain flips the order, and 11 (the whole tray) is not one of the numbers in this ratio at all.

questions.question: In Ms. Chan's Grade 6 class, 10 students ride the bus to school and 14 students walk. Which ratio compares bus riders to walkers?
questions.explain: Bus riders are named first, so their number comes first: 10 : 14. The one that says 10 : 24 uses the whole class (10 + 14) as the second number, but the question asks to compare one group with the other group, not with the total.

questions.question: Which of these means exactly the same thing as the ratio 7 to 2?
options: 2 to 7
questions.explain: The colon form keeps the same order as the word form, so 7 to 2 is written 7 : 2. Both versions that start with 2 reverse the comparison, and 9 : 2 comes from adding 7 + 2, which turns the comparison into a total.

questions.question: A cooler at soccer practice holds 20 juice boxes. 12 of them are lemon and the rest are berry. Which ratio compares berry juice boxes to lemon juice boxes?
questions.explain: First find the berry boxes: 20 - 12 = 8. Berry is named first, so the ratio is 8 : 12. The one that says 8 : 20 compares berry to all the juice boxes instead of berry to lemon.

questions.question: At an animal shelter, the ratio of cats to dogs is 9 : 12. Which sentence tells what this ratio means?
options: There are 21 cats at the shelter
For every 12 cats there are 9 dogs
There are 9 animals at the shelter altogether
For every 9 cats there are 12 dogs
questions.explain: Cats are named first in cats to dogs, so the 9 counts cats and the 12 counts dogs. Reading it as 12 cats and 9 dogs swaps the two groups, and 21 is the total number of animals, not the number of cats.

questions.question: In a swim class at the community centre there are 6 girls and 9 boys. Maya writes the ratio of girls to boys as 6 : 9. Ravi writes the same ratio as 9 : 6. Who is correct?
options: Maya, because girls are named first, so the number of girls is written first
Ravi, because the larger number is always written first in a ratio
Both are correct, because the order of the numbers in a ratio does not matter
Neither, because a ratio must compare one group to the whole class
questions.explain: The words girls to boys set the order, so the girl count 6 must come first: 6 : 9. Order really does change the meaning of a ratio, and there is no rule that the bigger number goes first.

questions.question: In a class of 28 students, 16 chose skating for the winter trip and the rest chose swimming. Emma says the ratio of swimmers to skaters is 16 : 12. What mistake did Emma make?
options: Nothing is wrong; 16 : 12 correctly compares swimmers to skaters
She wrote the two numbers in the wrong order; swimmers to skaters is 12 : 16
She should have compared swimmers to the whole class and written 12 : 28
She subtracted incorrectly; there are 14 swimmers, so it is 14 : 16
questions.explain: There are 28 - 16 = 12 swimmers, and swimmers are named first, so the ratio is 12 : 16. Emma kept the skating number in front, which is the most common slip: always match the first number to the group named first.

questions.question: A 650 g bag of trail mix is made of only raisins and almonds. There are 250 g of raisins in the bag. Which ratio compares the mass of almonds to the mass of raisins?
questions.explain: First find the almonds: 650 - 250 = 400 g. Almonds are named first, so the ratio is 400 : 250. The one that says 250 : 650 compares raisins to the whole bag, which is a part-to-whole comparison, not almonds to raisins.

questions.question: A park near Emily's school has 15 maple trees and 10 cedar trees, and no other trees. Which statement is correct?
options: The ratio of maple trees to cedar trees is 10 to 15
The ratio of maple trees to all the trees is 10 : 25
The ratio of cedar trees to maple trees is 15 : 10
The ratio of cedar trees to maple trees is 10 : 15
questions.explain: Cedar is named first in cedar to maple, so the cedar count 10 goes first: 10 : 15. Both statements that start with the wrong tree flip the comparison, and maple to all the trees would be 15 : 25, not 10 : 25.
